record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Can one develop a more effective collective-coordinate description of sine-Gordon scattering off a non-integrable boundary, despite the fact that the boundary interaction excites many additional modes?

evidence.quote: To this end, it would be nice to develop a more effective collective-coordinate description of the boundary situation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the sine-Gordon model on the half-line $x \le 0$ for a real scalar field $\phi(x,t)$ with bulk Lagrangian density
$$\mathcal{L} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_t\phi)^2 - \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x\phi)^2 - \frac{m^2}{\beta^2}\bigl(1-\cos(\beta\phi)\bigr),$$
supplemented at $x=0$ by a boundary potential
$$V_B(\phi(0,t)) = -M\cos\!\bigl(\tfrac{\beta}{2}(\phi(0,t)-\phi_0)\bigr),$$
giving the Robin-type boundary condition $\partial_x\phi(0,t) = -\tfrac{M\beta}{2}\sin\!\bigl(\tfrac{\beta}{2}(\phi(0,t)-\phi_0)\bigr)$. For generic values of the boundary parameters $(M,\phi_0)$ the boundary breaks the bulk integrability, and reflection of an incoming (anti)kink generically excites infinitely many radiative and breather modes in addition to producing reflected kinks/antikinks.

Develop an effective finite-dimensional collective-coordinate description of kink–boundary scattering in this non-integrable boundary sine-Gordon system: that is, construct a moduli space of field configurations parametrized by a finite set of coordinates (capturing kink position, possibly boundary-localized degrees of freedom, and the dominant excited modes), together with an induced metric and effective potential, such that the resulting reduced dynamics accurately reproduces the qualitative and quantitative features (reflection coefficients, kink/antikink/breather production thresholds as functions of incoming velocity and boundary parameters) of the full PDE dynamics, despite the proliferation of modes excited at the boundary.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., on sine-Gordon with Robin boundary conditions) has established the rich phenomenology of antikink reflection into kinks, antikinks, and multiple breathers in the non-integrable boundary case, and collective-coordinate methods have been applied successfully to related bulk problems (double sine-Gordon, modified sine-Gordon, kink-impurity interactions). However, no fully effective collective-coordinate reduction tailored to the boundary sine-Gordon problem that captures the many excited modes has been published; the problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Breaking integrability at the boundary: the sine-Gordon model with Robin boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: An antikink may be reflected into various combinations of an antikink, a kink, and one or more breathers, depending on the values of the initial antikink velocity and a parameter associated with the boundary condition.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes complex non-integrable boundary scattering phenomenology but does not provide a complete effective collective-coordinate description.

status_evidence.title: Collective coordinate analysis for double sine-Gordon model
status_evidence.snippet: Collective coordinate analysis for adding a space dependent potential to the double sine-Gordon model.
status_evidence.claim: Collective-coordinate methods exist for related bulk non-integrable problems, but not specifically for boundary sine-Gordon.
